nodes.strategy: M^(a,b) is the permutation representation on tabloids; tabloids of shape (a,b) are in equivariant bijection with the coset space S_(a+b)/(S_a x S_b). Induction of the trivial representation along an injective homomorphism into a finite group is the permutation representation on cosets. Build the equivariant bijection explicitly and transport it with FDRep.ofMulActionEquiv, which the module already provides.

nodes.strategy: Pure combinatorics, no representation theory. Write r = min k (n-k). For the weight (n-r, r) a semistandard tableau has only the entries 0 and 1; strict columns put at most one 0 above one 1 in each column, and weak rows force row 0 to be 0^a 1^b and row 1 to be all 1s. Hence K_(shape,(n-r,r)) = 1 when shape = (n-i, i) with i <= r and 0 otherwise. Recover i from a shape as shape.rowLen 1 to define the forward map, and send i to the unique tableau of shape (n-i, i) for the inverse.

nodes.strategy: Pure combinatorics. Introduce the first-column hook lengths l_i = mu.rowLen i + (m - 1 - i) for a row bound m. Prove that the hook lengths in row i are exactly {1,...,l_i} minus {l_i - l_j : j > i}, giving hookProduct = prod l_i! / prod_(i<j) (l_i - l_j). Prove independently that the number of standard tableaux satisfies the corner recursion f(mu) = sum over corners of f(mu - c), and that n! * prod (l_i - l_j) / prod l_i! satisfies the same recursion, which reduces to a Vandermonde-style polynomial identity. Conclude by induction on n.

verification.note: Proved in SymmetricGroupRep/Distinctness.lean. YoungDiagram.Dominates and its antisymmetry were added next to YoungDiagramOfSize. The dominance lemma counts labels: the first j rows of a nu-tabloid hold sum over i < j of nu.rowLen i labels, each column c of a mu-tableau holds at most min (mu.colLen c) j of them, and summing that bound over columns counts the cells of mu in its first j rows. The hypothesis of the counting lemma is supplied by the sign eigenvector property, which an isomorphism transports from Sagan's Lemma 2.3.3(4) on the source polytabloid.

nodes.strategy: Completeness by counting. The Specht modules are pairwise non-isomorphic simples indexed by YoungDiagramOfSize n. Over C the number of isomorphism classes of simple representations of a finite group equals the number of conjugacy classes, and conjugacy classes of Equiv.Perm (Fin n) are classified by cycle type, hence by partitions of n. A bijection YoungDiagramOfSize n = Nat.Partition n then forces the Specht list to be exhaustive.

api_reconnaissance.categorical_route: mathlib has CategoryTheory.exists_simple_subobject with simpleSubobject, simpleSubobjectArrow, a Mono instance and a Simple instance, all gated on IsArtinianObject X. That would give the induction step directly. BUT: `example (V : SymmetricGroupRepresentation n) : IsArtinianObject V := by infer_instance` FAILS - no instance exists for FDRep, and supplying one means building an order embedding from Subobject V into the submodules of a finite-dimensional space. Rejected as the primary route.
api_reconnaissance.module_route: Preferred. Work at the Representation/Submodule level, where mathlib does have support: MonoidAlgebra.instIsSemisimpleModule (Maschke, gated on NeZero (Nat.card G : k)), IsSemisimpleModule.exists_sSupIndep_sSup_simples_eq_top, IsSemisimpleModule.exists_linearEquiv_fin_dfinsupp, and the whole isotypic-component development in RingTheory/SimpleModule/Isotypic.lean (isotypicComponent, isotypicComponents, sSup_isotypicComponents, IsIsotypic.linearEquiv_fun). Transport to FDRep only at the end, via Representation.Equiv and Action.mkIso, which is the pattern already used in this repository by FDRep.ofMulActionEquiv and by spechtModule_singleRow.
api_reconnaissance.corroboration: This is also what TauCeti does: its development lives in Representation/Submodule rather than FDRep, which is independent evidence that the module level is the tractable one.
api_reconnaissance.splitting: Maschke as a splitting is available categorically without the Artinian route: mathlib provides `instance [NeZero (Nat.card G : k)] (V : FDRep k G) : Injective V`, and Injective.factorThru retracts any mono into V. Useful for the final assembly even if the induction happens at module level.

source_pack_issues.issue: The bundled file is the 22-page arXiv:1401.3826v3 paper 'Quantum Adversary Lower Bound for Element Distinctness with Small Range', not the 181-page thesis that .claude/reference-pdfs/README.md describes. It contains no Section 1.4.2 and no Lemma 1.12.
source_pack_issues.resolution: Both cited passages were verified against a correct copy of the thesis found elsewhere on this machine. Page references recorded here are for the real thesis (pdf page = printed page + 13). The Lean docstrings need no change; the reference pack does.

source_pack_issues.issue: The bundled copy is the 10 January 2011 draft, which uses flat per-chapter numbering (Theorem 3.1, Corollary 3.7, Theorem 4.25). The Lean docstrings cite the published edition's numbering (4.1.1, 4.2.4, 4.5.4, 3.10.2), which does not resolve in this file.
source_pack_issues.resolution: Mapping recorded per node: 4.1.1(ii) is Theorem 3.1(ii) p.33; 4.2.4 is Corollary 3.7 p.35; 3.10.2 (products) is Theorem 4.25 p.54; there is no analogue of 4.5.4, only an unnumbered Peter-Weyl remark on p.68. Docstrings are left untouched because they cite the published edition correctly.

source_pack_issues.issue: Pieri is never named in Sagan 2e; a full-text search over all 254 pages returns zero hits, and there is no horizontal-strip or vertical-strip exercise in Section 4.11.
source_pack_issues.resolution: Both Pieri nodes are derived as the one-row and one-column specialisations of Theorem 4.9.4, which is exactly how the dependency graph already routes them.

source_pack_issues.issue: Rosmanis Lemma 1.12 is stated without proof. The thesis explicitly declines to introduce the determinantal form of the irreducibles or the general Littlewood-Richardson rule, which is what a proof would need.
source_pack_issues.resolution: This target has no proof in its cited source, so it must be proved here from the Littlewood-Richardson rule and the branching rule. The thesis's Corollary 1.13, a special case, is proved from the branching rule and is the model to follow. Recorded as the highest-risk node.

source_pack_issues.issue: A source hunt recommended Ballantine-Orellana Theorem 2.1 as a proved replacement for Rosmanis Lemma 1.12, claiming it holds for an arbitrary second partition. That is false. Theorem 2.1 assumes lambda_1 - lambda_2 >= 2p, and the hypothesis is load-bearing in the proof. Instantiating it at lambda = (n-j, j) needs n - 2j >= 2i, which the Lean target's hypotheses (2i < n, 2j < n) do not imply: i = j = floor(n/2) - 1 satisfies the target and violates Ballantine-Orellana. The theorem is strictly narrower than the Lean statement, not more general.
source_pack_issues.resolution: Target stays UNSOURCED and must be proved here. The usable fragment is an intermediate display in the proof on printed page 17, s_(n-p,p) * s_lambda = sum over mu of size p of s_mu * s_(lambda/mu) minus the same sum over mu of size p-1, which carries no hypothesis on lambda. Its own inputs are cited to Macdonald and Stanley EC2 and are not proved in Ballantine-Orellana, so that display is itself 'states but does not prove'. Planned route: two-row Young's rule gives M^(m-k,k) as the sum of S^(m-j,j) for j <= k with all two-row Kostka numbers equal to one, which is the already-converted twoRowKostkaIndexEquiv; the determinantal identity then telescopes without Jacobi-Trudi.
